subject: high cpu load after upgrade to shiny 0.11

messages.author: fc439899b88457c2
messages.subject: high cpu load after upgrade to shiny 0.11
parts:
Hi,

After an upgrade to shiny 0.11, my shiny app started to eat up a significant amount of CPU.  I have the version of app installed on server, where the shiny is not updated, hence the comparison. My app is quite heavy, with lots of controls based on which a ggvis plot is modified, so maybe it is  a problem of my app.

With a new version CPU load on idle app (nothing is used) is about 40%, compared to 3-4% for and old version. I've tested this both on Safari and Firefox running on Mac OS X Mavericks (10.9.5). I also run R 3.1.1.

How in general I should proceed to find out which component exactly is eating up the CPU in a shiny app?

Vaidotas

messages.author: ca443e6eaa0e78ed
messages.subject: Re: high cpu load after upgrade to shiny 0.11
parts:
You could try using R's built-in profiling: http://adv-r.had.co.nz/Profiling.html

If it is really pathological you may be able to use my stackdump package (devtools::install_github("jcheng5/stackdump")). You would do stackdump::init(quit=FALSE) at the beginning of your app (say in a global.R), then on the server call "kill -SIGQUIT pid" where pid is the process ID of the Shiny process. This will cause the current execution stack to be printed to stderr. If you're using Shiny Server then you can view the logs at /var/log/shiny-server/*.log to see what is being computed each time you call kill.
